https://www.dw.com/en/sweden-one-killed-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JD8f Police identified the suspected attacker as an 18-year-old man Image: Philip O’Connor/REUTERS Advertisement A person armed with a sword has wounded multiple people at a school in Fagersta in central Sweden , authorities said Friday. Police said one person had been taken into custody and there was no longer any danger to the public. After initially saying three people had been wounded in the attack, two of them severely, police later said an additional person had been killed. Earlier on Friday, Sweden's healthcare authority said two boys, both aged between 12 and 17, were being treated in hospital. Police said the suspect was an 18-year-old man, whom they shot during a confrontation and took into custody. What else do we know? Police were called to the Brinellskola, a secondary school in Fagersta, at around 2 p.m. local time (1200 GMT). The school, which has some 450 students aged 16 to 20, had just reopened after the summer holidays. Public broadcaster SVT reported that ambulances, police cars and a police helicopter were outside the property. The municipality said other schools and some public buildings in the area had been locked down. Fagersta, home to some 12,000 people, lies around 170 kilometers (105 miles) northwest of the capital, Stockholm. Police locked down other schools in the area following the attack Image: Niklas Hagman/TT/picture alliance Reactions to 'terrible news' "Our thoughts are with all those affected," Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said in a post on X. "We do not yet know what lies behind the act, but we know that the police are working very intensively." Magdalena Andersson, leader of the opposition Social Democrats, lamented the "terrible news." "When violence takes place at a school, I know it impacts everyone in our country. All of Sweden ⁠stands together with Fagersta at this difficult time," she wrote on X. Other attacks at educational institutions Sweden has seen a number of high-profile attacks at educational facilities in recent years. In February 2025, a 35-year-old man killed 10 people at an adult education center in Orebro. In another incident, an 18-year-old student fatally stabbed two teachers at a Malmo high school in March 2022. Don't let the algorithm hide the news. https://www.oneindia.com/international/t.text: Police have found three bodies inside the home of a 25-year-old man accused of killing six people in a shooting in Poland. The discovery has added another shocking development to Saturdays attack in Krakow, where several people were also injured after a gunman opened fire in a crowded area.Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the three people found dead were believed to be members of the suspects family. The bodies of two women and one man were found at his house in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, around 200 km from Krakow.Police Find Three Bodies At Gunmans HousePolice reached the suspects home hours after the shooting. Officers first used a drone to check the property as they believed that weapons and other dangerous items could be inside.We know that a significant amount of weaponry may be inside the house, Tusk said.Residents of the building were evacuated before counterterrorism officers entered the house. Polands Internal Security Agency and Military Counterintelligence Service are also helping police with the investigation.Gunman Opens Fire In Crowded Krakow SquareThe attack took place shortly before 3 pm in Krakows historic Main Market Square, a popular place among tourists and local residents.Police said the suspect arrived in a car and started firing at people randomly. Several people ran for cover as gunshots rang out across the busy square.A tram passing through the area was also hit during the shooting. Its windows were shattered, but no passengers were injured.Police officers reached the spot and confronted the gunman within three minutes of receiving the first report. They shot him during an exchange of fire and arrested him.Six People Killed, 16 Taken To HospitalThe shooting killed six people, including four women and two men. One of the victims was a British national.A total of 16 people, including five foreign nationals, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The injured foreign nationals were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia.Both police officers underwent surgery. One officer was in a very critical condition after being shot three times while trying to stop the attacker.Police Investigate Suspects Far-Right LinksPolice have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish national. He was reportedly wearing military-style clothes and using an AR-15 rifle. Officers also found several weapons and ammunition inside his car.Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said the initial findings showed that the suspect may have been influenced by far-right ideology.Everything points to the fact that the shooter was influenced by far-right ideology, a matter that will also be subject to investigation, Kierwinski told reporters.The suspect is currently in hospital and is in a stable but critical condition after undergoing multiple surgeries. Investigators are looking into his possible links with far-right groups and the reason behind the attack.Prime Minister Tusk visited Krakow after the shooting and described the incident as an unprecedented act of violence in Poland.Until now in Poland we havent had such drastic cases of terrorism...thats what we have to call this cruel attack on peoples lives here in Krakow.
